shortDescription: Chinese imports of soybeans from the United States fell 12% in August from a year earlier, as most of the 12 million metric tons of soybeans China purchased late last year, following a summit in Busan, South Korea, have already arrived at ports in recent months.

children: Chinese imports of soybeans from the United States fell 12% in August from a year earlier, as most of the 12 million metric tons of soybeans China purchased late last year, following a summit in Busan, South Korea, have already arrived at ports in recent months.
China imported 200,477 metric tons of soybeans from the United States in August, down from 227,205 tons in the same month of 2025, data from the General Administration of Customs showed on Sunday.
Imports from Brazil rose 1% year-on-year to 10.61 million tons from 10.48 million tons in August last year.
China, the world's largest soybean buyer, brought in 12.14 million metric tons in August, down 1.1% from 12.28 million tons a year earlier and up 5.7% from July.
In the January-August period, soybean imports from the U.S. fell 34% from a year earlier to 10.66 million tons, while shipments from Brazil rose 5% to 55.14 million tons.
China had also passed the halfway mark toward its 25 million-ton U.S. soybean purchase target for this year, with shipments beginning in September.
Trade tensions between Beijing and Washington last year had prompted Chinese buyers to delay purchases of the previous U.S. harvest until after an October summit between the two countries' leaders.
Following the meeting, Beijing purchased around 12 million tons of U.S. soybeans, still well below levels from before the trade war.

Traders told Reuters last week that China had passed the halfway mark toward its commitment to buy 25 million metric tons of U.S. soybeans in 2026, a pledge agreed with Washington last October and reaffirmed in May.
Traders hope the summit between U.S. Presidents Donald Trump and China's President Xi Jinping next week will provide greater clarity on China's future demand for U.S. soybeans.
